title: A lookup revalidation whose search or candidate page answers an HTTP error falls back to the offline stamp instead of printing not found
goal: Found by the SP-tm4wlsve review (ST-mq7we5r2): the revalidation's lost flag is set only by provider.spent() or provider.failures(), and failures() counts only requests with no HTTP answer (provider.py:291; factdiff.py:858-863, :1029-1054, :1315, :1332). A 429 or 5xx from the provider's search API or a candidate page yields [] or (None, None) in search_urls and page_doc, and elsewhere returns no candidate page, so a moved passage prints [not found DATE]. An HTTP error of the search or a candidate page counts as a failure: the line keeps the offline stamp and the source's note names the request; a stubbed pack_revalidate case where learn.microsoft.com/api/search answers 503 for an edited, unfound passage expects no outcome and the note.

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 7 of 19, "Freshness at lookup: revalidation on HTTP errors, soft 404s, unreachable hosts and a changed registry"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed. Premise: with a page whose edited passage is gone and learn.microsoft.com/api/search answering 503, revalidate prints [not found]. Run 2026-10-12 on the base with stubbed provider.request (a page that dropped one passage, the search 503): reproduces, outcome 'not found' after 3 requests. Fix in factdiff.lookup_source's lost flag and search_urls/page_doc (provider.failures() counts only no-answer requests): an HTTP error of the search or a candidate page counts as a failure. The check names a test that does not exist yet (collects none): the worker extends the pack_revalidate test case and puts revalidate_search_http_error in its name, adding no new test id. kb/_self/tools.md line of 'Revalidation at question time' lists the causes of the offline stamp: add the HTTP error.
